question: Mahesh bought some sharpeners at the rate of ₹150 a dozen. He sold them for ₹41 each. His profit percentage is ______%.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert both to a single item unit for direct comparison:

Cost Price (CP) of 1 sharpener = 150 ÷ 12 = ₹12.5

Selling Price (SP) of 1 sharpener = ₹41

Profit % = ((SP − CP) ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ ((41 − 12.5) ÷ 12.5) × 100 = (28.5 ÷ 12.5) × 100 = 228%

**∴ The correct answer is 228%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total CP of 1 dozen (12 sharpeners) = ₹150

SP of 1 sharpener = ₹41

**Formula Used:**

Total Profit = Total SP − Total CP

Profit % = (Total Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

 
 
 Total CP
 ₹150
 
 
 
 Total SP
 ₹492
 
 
 
• 
 

 
 
 Profit = ₹342
 + 228%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total SP for 1 dozen = 41 × 12 = ₹492

⇒ Total Profit = 492 − 150 = ₹342

⇒ Profit % = (342 ÷ 150) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 34.2 ÷ 15 × 100 = 2.28 × 100 = 228%

**∴ The correct answer is 228%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when Selling Price (SP) > Cost Price (CP). Profit % is always calculated on the CP unless explicitly stated otherwise: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is a reduction offered on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. Selling Price = MP − Discount. Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer uses a false weight, the actual CP corresponds to the false weight given, while SP corresponds to the claimed weight. Profit % = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.
